name: Step-by-Step Interlocking Garage Tile Installation Guide

step.name: Step 1: Empty and clean the entire garage area
step.text: Clear out all vehicles, workbenches, and stored storage containers so the entire concrete slab is visible. Sweep and vacuum away all loose sand, dirt, and dust, then degrease any oil spots to create a clean surface. The slab should be completely clear of debris before bringing tiles inside.

step.name: Step 2: Acclimate your garage tiles to room temperature
step.text: Bring all tile cartons inside the garage or an adjacent conditioned space at least 24 hours prior to starting work. Ensure the space stays at least 72°F so the material reaches thermal equilibrium. Acclimated tiles are flexible and will not buckle or fight you during locking.

step.name: Step 3: Measure the slab and set your entry baseline
step.text: Snap a chalk line near the garage overhead door to establish a straight, square starting point. Plan your grid layout from the entrance working backward, making sure the entry row aligns neatly with the garage door threshold. A centered layout avoids awkward thin slivers along visible entrance points.

step.name: Step 4: Interlock the tiles along your established grid
step.text: Connect the modular tiles row by row using a rubber mallet to seat the interlocking peg-and-loop joints securely. Keep all tile directional loops pointed the same way across the floor for a uniform fit. Work methodically from the front door back toward the rear wall.

step.name: Step 5: Trim perimeter tiles while preserving expansion gaps
step.text: Measure the remaining space along walls, posts, and built-in cabinets, then cut edge pieces with a fine-toothed saw. Leave a dedicated expansion gap around all fixed walls and vertical obstacles as recommended by the manufacturer. This spacing allows the floor to expand during summer heat without tenting.

step.name: Step 6: Install sloped entrance ramps and verify transitions
step.text: Attach manufacturer transition ramps along the garage door threshold to ensure smooth entry for vehicles and rolling toolboxes. Inspect the finished layout to verify no movement joints sit directly under wheel paths or stationary machinery.
